Beginner.learningGoal: Understand copy semantics of structs versus shared identity of classes.
gotchas: Assigning a class instance shares it; mutating through one name is visible through the other
A let struct cannot be mutated, a let class reference can still mutate its properties
mutating methods are required on structs to change stored properties
goodSolutionShows: Struct for plain data and class only where identity matters
mutating funcs on a struct, with tests proving the original is unchanged after a copy
shapeHints: a playlist model copied and edited independently
a shared counter class versus a value counter
a settings snapshot that must not change after being passed on

Intermediate.learningGoal: Reason about aliasing and equality when value types contain reference types.
gotchas: A struct containing a class property copies the reference, not the object
=== compares identity and only works on classes; == needs Equatable
Mutating a copy of an array of class instances still mutates the shared instances
goodSolutionShows: Deep-copy helper for a struct with a reference member
Identity checks with === only where they are meaningful
Tests that demonstrate which parts are shared after copying
shapeHints: a document struct holding a mutable style object
duplicating a shopping cart that holds item objects
detecting whether two views of a model share storage

Advanced.learningGoal: Implement copy-on-write for a value type wrapping reference storage.
gotchas: isKnownUniquelyReferenced must be called on an inout reference, and a stray extra reference makes it always false
Forgetting to copy before mutation makes copies share state
Copy-on-write must also apply to every mutating entry point, not just one
goodSolutionShows: Private storage class with isKnownUniquelyReferenced in each mutating method
Value semantics proven by mutating a copy and checking the original
Minimal copying when uniquely referenced, observable via a copy counter injected into the storage
shapeHints: a small buffer or text-rope type with append and subscript set
an immutable-looking Matrix wrapping a class storage
a history stack that shares storage until written

Expert.learningGoal: Build a copy-on-write value type over reference storage and prove its value semantics and copy avoidance with deterministic tests.
gotchas: isKnownUniquelyReferenced is false whenever another strong reference exists, including a local copy of the storage reference taken before the check
Every mutating entry point (append, insert, subscript set, remove) needs the uniqueness check, not just one of them
Accidental copies stay invisible unless the storage counts its own copies, for example when a loop re-reads the storage before each mutation
goodSolutionShows: A storage class copied only inside one makeUnique() helper that every mutator calls
Tests that count storage copies through an injected counter instead of timing anything
Value semantics asserted after chains of copy, mutate the original, mutate the copy
shapeHints: a copy-on-write text buffer with append, insert and a copy counter
an array wrapper with an undo history that shares storage until written
a Matrix whose copies share storage until one is written
